page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes instruction support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The instance provides no integrated local SSD storage, no discrete GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core compute capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2691.89 ranking in the top 25 percent. Multi-core throughput aligns with standard industry averages, reflected by a stress-ng multi-core score of 10798.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5419.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth measures 45.33 GB/sec for reads and 26.94 GB/sec for writes. The instance exhibits lower relative performance in heavy parallel decompression workloads, where bzip3 multi-threaded decompression yielded 27.85 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25 percent. Static web serving achieves 8.25 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 8.04 million operations per second.

The hardware resource density offers qualitative cost efficiency for balanced compute and memory demands that do not require local ephemeral disks or dedicated hardware acceleration. The standard memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it well suited for middle-tier enterprise applications, microservice host nodes, relational database instances relying on network storage, web application servers, and caching layers.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating on x86_64 architecture, it delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio without bundled local storage or GPUs. Compute benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core CPU performance, reaching the top 25 percent in stress-ng tests, alongside average multi-core and memory throughput scores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression represents a minor performance constraint, falling into the bottom 25 percent. With static web serving throughput reaching 8.25 GB/sec and Redis handling 8.04 million SET operations per second, the server provides balanced performance efficiency for general cloud workloads, containerized applications, web serving, and mid-sized database environments using external network storage.
